summary: Texas tower lit 1 Nov 1961 at the Buzzards Bay entrance, replacing lightships; rebuilt 1996-97 as a smaller structure; automated; not open to the public.

structures.note: Texas tower on four steel legs, steel piles filled with concrete; dismantled 1996 or 1997 (archive)
Replacement tower; the year is 1996 (LighthouseFriends) or 1996 or 1997 (archive)

access.note: The archive lists the station as not open to the public. It stands in open water; the only visitors LighthouseFriends describes came at the 1961 commissioning, by cutter, patrol boat and helicopter.

events.note: Steel Texas tower on four steel legs (steel piles filled with concrete), built by the Perini Corporation for $950,000; deck house and helicopter pad on top
Placed in operation November 1961; commissioned 1 November 1961 at 11:28, relieving the Buzzards Bay lightship
Ralph O. Morris first officer in charge; Lionel F. Crossman took over weeks later
October 1890 severe gale damages coast buoys; a whistling buoy off Hen and Chickens Reef goes adrift and comes ashore near Cuttyhunk (report for fiscal 1891)
February 1917 ice damages aids to navigation and lighthouse vessels, particularly in Buzzards Bay
Second tower replaces the 1961 tower (LighthouseFriends: 1996). The archive says the old tower was dismantled in 1996 or 1997 and replaced with a smaller structure.
Latest Coast Guard crew line in the archive: at least 1971

corrections.proposed: dismantled 1996 or 1997; replaced with a smaller structure
corrections.why: The archive's record for the 1961 tower says Existing: No and Disposition: Dismantled 1996 Or 1997 and Replaced with a Smaller Structure. The present structure is a different tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record says the structure is gone (USLHS) and OpenStreetMap maps a structure today. Both are right: the 1961 Texas tower was dismantled in 1996 or 1997, and the smaller tower that replaced it is the one on the map.
The 1961 tower is the Texas tower built by Perini; the 1996 or 1997 structure is the replacement. LighthouseFriends gives 1996 for the replacement; the archive gives 1996 or 1997.

notes_for_editor: 1) Replacement year: LighthouseFriends says 1996; the archive says dismantled 1996 or 1997; Rowlett's record gives 1997 for Tower 2; the story gives both sources and does not choose. The Coast Guard Historian's page (history.uscg.mil), which gives 'Year Current Tower(s) First Lit: 1997' in a search snippet, could not be read (403 live; the Internet Archive capture returns only the wrapper), so it is not cited. 2) Depth and height: LighthouseFriends gives 61 ft of water and 117 ft above the water for the light's exhibition; the record's focal height is 20.4 m (about 67 ft) and its water depth is not given. Wikipedia (not cited) gives 50 ft of water. Not resolved. 3) Automation date: the record's Wikidata gives 1980; the archive's crew lines run to at least 1971; LighthouseFriends says an automated tower marks the location today and gives no date. The story gives no automation date. 4) Lightship identity: LighthouseFriends names the Buzzards Bay, Hens & Chickens and Vineyard Sound lightships as the predecessors. Our sources number the Hen and Chickens vessel No. 2 (LHB 1891 and 1893), No. 42 (Bulletin 1914) and No. 86 (Bulletin 1939). We did not establish which vessel was relieved in 1961, nor the Buzzards Bay lightship's number. The story speaks of 'the station's vessel' only. Wikipedia's LV-5 and LV-10 designations are not used. 5) Roster: matched by name and position to the USLHS place 'Buzzards Bay Entrance Light' (0.13 km). The roster has a 1919 to 1921 'Lamp Lighter', Henry R. Holt, who predates the tower by about forty years. The archive does not say what he tended, and our corpus does not name him; he is not attributed to the tower in the story. A human should check his line against the archive's own record before any use. 6) Roster role: 'Principal Lighthouse Keeper' normalised to 'keeper' (sole) by the roster tool, since there is no assistant line for the tower. 7) Corpus OCR: the 1891 entry reads 'Hen and ChieJcens Light-Vessel^ Ko, 2' in the OCR; the story corrects this and the 1917 'weD' and 'vessols' silently. Evidence quotes keep the OCR text exactly. The 1891 scan p. 65 and 67 entries are in the report for fiscal 1891 (title page at scan p. 6); the 1893 entry at scan p. 70 is in the report for fiscal 1893. 8) No wreck or rescue at the tower itself appears in the sources read. A Chronicling America search for 'Hen and Chickens' with 'lightship' in Massachusetts, 1890 to 1913, returned yacht-race reports only, so no newspaper pages are cited. 9) The Commissioner's fiscal 1918 'Purpose' passage is at scan p. 386, read from the corpus text; the page image was not viewed. 10) The story's quotations from the Board's 1891 and 1893 reports and the 1917 Commissioner report are short and from public-domain government reports. LighthouseFriends is used for facts and only short phrases are quoted. 11) Fact-check 2026-10-27: the story no longer identifies the Hen and Chickens No. 2 vessel with the later numbers. The 1939 entry 'Hen and Chickens Lightship No. 86' prints no state, and the 1918 Bulletin (PDF p. 16) also lists a 'Great Round Shoal Light Vessel No. 86, Mass.'; these are not tied to the 1961 station. 12) The archive's record for the 1961 tower gives 'Active Aid to Navigation?: No'; the story does not use this field.
